# ColorSchemeProvider

Keeps the page's color scheme: it applies the person's choice (`light`, `dark` or `system`) as the `.dark` class on `<html>`, which is how shadcn themes switch, keeps it in `localStorage`, and follows the system's setting live while the choice is `system`. Every `ColorSchemeToggle` and `useColorScheme` under it share its options.

```tsx
import { ColorSchemeProvider } from "@/registry/ouro/lib/ouro/color-scheme";
```

## Example

```tsx
// app/root.tsx (React Router):
<html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning>
  <head>
    <script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: colorSchemeScript() }} />
  </head>
  <body>
    <ColorSchemeProvider>
      <Outlet />
    </ColorSchemeProvider>
  </body>
</html>
```

## Usage

Wrap the app once, in the root layout, and put `colorSchemeScript()` in `<head>` so the first paint already has the scheme. Ouro UI components need neither: without them, dark mode is whatever `.dark` class the app sets.

## Props

Type: `ColorSchemeProviderProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | Your app, or the part of it that shows the scheme. |
| `defaultScheme` | `"system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"system"` | The scheme before a person chooses one. |
| `storageKey` | `string` | `"ouro-color-scheme"` | The `localStorage` key that keeps the choice. |
